content:
Requirement R07 (input): Report Surveillance Event. Fixed modalities: Touch and Keyboard. Intent: Allow the pilot to report a surveillance event as it happens..

We will design this requirement in three sequential layers, all within THIS conversation: Function first, then Behaviour, then Structure. Conduct the sequence yourself — when a layer is agreed, state its final label clearly and move to the next.
- Functions: propose 2-3 genuinely distinct candidates labeled F-07.1, F-07.2, ... Distinct means each opens a different interaction goal — not the same goal reworded.
- Behaviours: 2-3 distinct interaction flows, labeled Be-07.<F>.1, Be-07.<F>.2, ... using the closed F index.
- Structures: 2-3 distinct sets of concrete HMI elements, labeled S-07.<F>.<Be>.1, ... using the closed F and Be indices.

Start with the Function candidates now (state the intent back first). The designer closes the whole requirement at the end.

**Intent:** Enable the pilot to report a surveillance event to C2 the moment it is observed, in flight.

Function candidates:

**F-07.1 — Pilot commits an observed surveillance event to C2.**
The teleology: the artefact exists to get a detected event out of the cockpit and into the C2 report channel. Measurable effect: an event report is transmitted and acknowledged.

**F-07.2 — Pilot classifies/qualifies the reported event.**
Distinct goal: not just "an event happened" but *what kind* — attaching event type/attributes to the report. Opens a categorization interaction rather than a commit interaction.

**F-07.3 — Pilot geo-anchors the event to its observed location.**
Distinct goal: tie the report to a POI/AOI on the map so C2 receives *where* it occurred, not just that it occurred.

---

Note on distinctness vs R05: R05 (F-05.1) already covers *submit structured intel reports to C2* via the map-anchored press-and-hold pattern. F-07.3 here risks collapsing into R05's goal — geo-anchoring + commit is essentially the same interaction pattern already closed. I'd flag **F-07.3 as a likely reuse of R05's Behaviour/Structure**, not a genuinely new Function.

That leaves F-07.1 (commit) and F-07.2 (classify) as the genuinely distinct pair. The tension in this requirement is *speed* — "as it happens" implies a low-friction one-action commit (F-07.1) may conflict with the richer classification of F-07.2.

My recommendation: close on **F-07.1** as the primary Function, treating classification as a possible sub-behaviour rather than a separate Function unless you want event-typing to be a first-class goal.

Which way do you want to go?
